result.topic_en: Gauss derives the second-order differential equation satisfied by the series y = x^{-1} + (1/4)x^{-3} + ..., transforms it by the substitutions x = (t + 1/t)/2 and x = 1/p, and deduces the functional relation φ((t+1/t)/2) = 2t φ(tt).
result.transcription:
Math 27 [-47a[?] 2-] (2)
Ponendo
$y = x^{-1} + \frac{1}{4}x^{-3} + \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{9}{16}x^{-5} + \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{9}{16}\cdot\frac{25}{36}x^{-9}$ etc. $(=\varphi x$
eruitur
$xy + (3xx-1)\frac{dy}{dx} + x(xx-1)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0$
Iam ponendo $x = \frac{1}{2}(t+t^{-1})$ erit
$\frac{dt}{dx} = [-\frac{1}{?}-]\frac{2}{1-t^{-2}}$ $\qquad \frac{4t^{-3}}{(1-t^{-2})^2}$
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{dt}\cdot\frac{2}{1-t^{-2}}$
$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \left(\frac{2}{1-t^{-2}}\right)^2\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} - \frac{1}{t^3}\left(\frac{2}{1-t^{-2}}\right)^3\frac{dy}{dt}$
Hinc
$\frac{tt+1}{2t}y + \frac{3t^4+2tt+3}{2tt-2}\cdot\frac{dy}{dt} + \frac{tt+1}{2t}\left(\frac{tt-1}{2t}\right)^2\left(\left(\frac{2tt}{tt-1}\right)^2\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} - \left(\frac{2t}{tt-1}\right)^3\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$
sive
$\frac{tt+1}{2t}y + \frac{3t^4+1}{2tt-2}\frac{dy}{dt} + \frac{t(tt+1)}{2}\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = 0$
sive
$(t^4-1)y + t(3t^4+1)\frac{dy}{dt} + tt(t^4-1)\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = 0$
Hinc facile deducitur
$y = 2(t^{-1} + \frac{1}{4}t^{-5} + \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{9}{16}t^{-9} + \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{9}{16}\cdot\frac{25}{36}t^{-13} + $ etc.$)$
sive
$\varphi\,\frac{1}{2}(t+\frac{1}{t}) = 2t\,\varphi\,tt$
Ponendo $x = \frac{1}{p}$ erit
$y - p(1+pp)\frac{dy}{dp} + pp(1-pp)\frac{d^2y}{dp^2} = 0$

methods.what: Power series in 1/x defining the function φ(x)
Second-order linear ODE satisfied by the series
Change of variable x = (t+1/t)/2 and the transformed first and second derivatives (chain rule)
Transformed ODE in the variable t
Series solution of the transformed equation in t
ODE transformed by the substitution x = 1/p
